title: Cadence load mapper: deterministic throughput harness and customer acceptance checklist
creator: Anika Shah
description:
Goal: deliver a deterministic, tenant-aware load testing harness (Cadence) and an associated benchmarking methodology that product, eng, and SRE can use to sign off Dedicated capacity throughput guarantees for customers. This ticket covers architecture decisions for the harness, concrete benchmark scenarios, telemetry schema, acceptance gates for customer sign-off, and an initial set of customer-facing artifacts (how-to, examples, and a GitHub prober).

Why different: earlier work focused on broad acceptance suites and stress orchestration. Cadence's aim is to provide reproducible, time-series aligned 'cadence profiles' (ramp, steady-state, microburst windows) that map to real tenant mixes and autoscaler interactions so we can reason about throughput guarantees across policy permutations.

Scope: prototype harness, one benchmark pack for small/medium/large tenant mixes, telemetry dashboard template, acceptance checklist for Solutions/Customer Onboarding, and a follow-up plan to integrate with Dedicated onboarding automation.
harness_architecture:
Cadence is a modular harness with three components: (1) Profile Engine - encodes cadence profiles (sequence of QPS targets, concurrency, token-distribution, and seq-length mix), (2) Orchestrator - schedules multi-tenant probes across a fleet of prober workers, handles failure injection and autoscaler signals, (3) Collector - emits standardized telemetry (per-request latency quantiles, per-token cost, queue-depth, GPU-util, KV-cache hit rates, and autoscaler events) to our metrics/trace backend. The harness runs as a self-contained k8s job for local verification and as a distributed fleet for full-system benchmarks.

Implementation notes: use gosdk/prober for the lightweight prober client, protobuf-based profile manifests for reproducibility, and the orchestration layer will be a thin Go service with a pluggable driver to replay real traces or synthetic mixes.
test_plan:
Phase 1: unit and local integration tests for Profile Engine and Collector (target: 2 weeks). Phase 2: run canonical benchmark packs against a dedicated staging cluster to validate repeatability (3 runs minimum per pack) and collect baseline metrics. Phase 3: run tenant-mix + autoscaler interaction tests that exercise scale-up/scale-down hysteresis and burst windows. Phase 4: customer acceptance runs with Solutions and feature-flagged policies. Each run produces a canonical evidence bundle (prometheus exports, raw logs, topology snapshot, and prober traces) and a signed checklist.

Sample CLI: cadence run --profile small-tenant-mix --repeats 3 --out bundle.tar.gz

Gates: median token latency within SLO, 95th % CPU/GPU utilization below configured alert thresholds during steady state, no >1% failed requests in steady-state window, autoscaler must not have oscillated more than 2 scale events per 5 minutes during steady-state.
acceptance_criteria: Three repeatable benchmark runs whose steady-state token throughput falls within ±3%
Tail latency (p99) is <= declared SLA for the profile
Autoscaler behavior documented and within allowed oscillation thresholds
Evidence bundle uploaded to Drive and linked in the ticket
Solutions engineering has completed a joint customer run and signed the checklist
